cross_check.method: One direct HTTPS GET of the official DCP Zoning Resolution portal HTML for this section (sha256 and byte count pinned in source) and one GET of its print/PDF render (raw_pdf_sha256 and byte count pinned here). The verbatim excerpt was extracted PROGRAMMATICALLY from the raw HTML bytes (the field--name-body container): defined terms (bold-italic <strong><em>) written #term#; ordered-list items prefixed with the label the print/PDF render prints ((a),(b) for the outer list; (1),(2) for a nested list; (i),(ii) for a third level); runs of whitespace and non-breaking spaces collapsed to one space and each block trimmed; embedded figures omitted. The resulting text was then compared character-for-character with the text drawn in the print/PDF (whitespace and non-breaking spaces removed on both sides). Result recorded in cross_check.result.

verbatim_excerpt:
23-231 Floor area provisions for amenities

Floor space in a #building# allocated to #residential# amenities may be exempted from the definition of #floor area#, in an amount not to exceed five percent of the #residential floor area# of the #building#.

Such amenities may include recreation spaces, including those required pursuant to Section 23-63, or other amenities, including, but not be limited to, co-working areas, library or reading rooms, or music practice rooms, package or storage rooms, laundry facilities, or pet-related facilities.

However, amenity space shall not include floor space for circulation through the #building#, including, corridors or vertical circulation spaces.

Amenities provided pursuant to this Section shall be accessible to the residents of the #building#.
verbatim_excerpt_composition: Verbatim blocks joined by a blank line, in page order: [0] the displayed section number and title; then each body paragraph and list item. A list item is written with the label the print/PDF render prints in front of it ((a),(b) outer; (1),(2) nested; (i),(ii) third level), followed by one space; an item's heading line and its text (a double line break in the HTML) are separate blocks. Defined terms (bold-italic in the HTML) are written #term#. Runs of whitespace and non-breaking spaces are written as one space and each block is trimmed; no word was changed. The structured labels were confirmed against the print/PDF render (cross_check: match).
